newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki sharply off after Wall St weakness.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki sharply off after Wall St weakness.

text.p: Shares on Friday finally made a clear downward correction, surrendering to unexpected overnight falls in Wall Street in quite a dramatic reversal after the index again scaled new heights on Thursday.
The HEX fell 1.79 percent at 2,736.12 points, down about one percent on the week.

Although brokers said the fall was a solid prompt for fears the equities rally may have hit its limits, some noted that the correction was less drastic than had been feared, and volumes looked calm -- 555.8 million markka with 40 percent in Nokia.
With the bourse more or less split between a fall in Nokia and further gains in insurer Pohjola, much depends for next week on the U.S. which Finland is likely to track, brokers said.
Nokia was hit by tech losses in Wall Street and booked a 14.00 markka or four percent closing loss at 316.50.

Pohjola powered ahead, rising 9.50 or over seven percent in solid trade to 141.50 in a carry-through of bullishness after Thursday's news it would bring its fast-growing life-insurance business into the publicly traded group, brokers said.

Raisio fell 6.00 markka to 409.00, still weak on a newspaper report on Thursday that a Finnish inventor had sought a patent for a cholesterol-reducing substance which the paper dubbed a "challenger" to the fat-soluble cholesterol cutter in Raisio's Benecol margarine.
Suunto fell after warning its third tertial sales had been weaker than expected, and its full-year 1996 pre-tax profit would be between 12 and 14 million markka.
Forestries were soft after the U.S. forestries index fell over two percent overnight.
